# 4-Bar Harmonization

## A Minor

**Bar 1:** Am (i) for the full bar
**Bar 2:** F (VI) on beat 1–2, then C (III) on beat 3–4
**Bar 3:** Dm (iv) on beat 1–2, then E (V) on beat 3–4
**Bar 4 (authentic cadence):** E (V) on beat 1–2, then Am (i) on beat 3–4

**LH voicings (smooth voice-leading):**
Bar 1: A₂ – C₃ – E₃ (Am root position).
Bar 2, beat 1: A₂ – C₃ – F₃ (F first inversion, the C stays, E moves up to F). Beat 3: G₂ – C₃ – E₃ (C first inversion, smooth drop in the bass).
Bar 3, beat 1: A₂ – D₃ – F₃ (Dm root position). Beat 3: G#₂ – B₂ – E₃ (E root position, first inversion works too).
Bar 4: E₂ – G#₂ – B₂ resolving to A₂ – C₃ – E₃.

**Plagal alternative for bar 4:** Replace E (V) with Dm (iv) on beat 1–2, then Am (i) on beat 3–4. LH: D₂ – F₂ – A₂ resolving to A₂ – C₃ – E₃. This is softer and suits a reflective mood.

**RH melody across all four bars:**
Bar 1: C – E – G – A (eighth notes filling the bar).
Bar 2: G – E – C – E (the motif turning back on itself).
Bar 3: D – F – A – G# (leading into the dominant).
Bar 4: A – E – A (quarter, quarter, half — landing on the tonic).

---

## C Minor

**Bar 1:** Cm (i) for the full bar
**Bar 2:** Ab (VI) on beat 1–2, then Eb (III) on beat 3–4
**Bar 3:** Fm (iv) on beat 1–2, then G (V) on beat 3–4
**Bar 4 (authentic cadence):** G (V) on beat 1–2, then Cm (i) on beat 3–4

**LH voicings:**
Bar 1: C₂ – Eb₂ – G₂ (Cm root position).
Bar 2, beat 1: C₂ – Eb₂ – Ab₂ (Ab first inversion, Eb stays). Beat 3: Bb₁ – Eb₂ – G₂ (Eb first inversion).
Bar 3, beat 1: Ab₁ – C₂ – F₂ (Fm first inversion). Beat 3: G₁ – B₁ – D₂ (G root position, B natural for harmonic minor).
Bar 4: G₁ – B₁ – D₂ resolving to C₂ – Eb₂ – G₂.

**Plagal alternative for bar 4:** Fm (iv) on beat 1–2, then Cm (i) on beat 3–4. LH: F₁ – Ab₁ – C₂ resolving to C₂ – Eb₂ – G₂.

**RH melody:**
Bar 1: C – Eb – G – Ab (eighth notes).
Bar 2: G – Eb – C – Eb.
Bar 3: F – Ab – C – B (B natural, leading tone).
Bar 4: C – G – C (quarter, quarter, half — landing home).

---

# Solo Piano Arrangement in A Minor (Wedding, 12 Bars)

This is in 4/4, moderate tempo (around 72–80 bpm), gentle and lyrical. The RH plays the motif and variations. The LH uses a simple broken-chord pattern throughout: bass note on beat 1, then two upper chord tones alternating on beats 2, 3, and 4 (like a slow Alberti but without rushing). Think of the LH pattern as: low note – middle – high – middle, all eighth notes, two per beat.

### Bars 1–4: Statement

**Bar 1 — Am (i)**
RH: C₄ – E₄ – G₄ – A₄ (eighth notes, then a quarter rest or let A ring)
LH: A₂ – E₃ – C₃ – E₃ – A₂ – E₃ – C₃ – E₃ (steady broken chord, all eighths)

**Bar 2 — Am (i)**
RH: G₄ – E₄ – C₄ – E₄ (eighth notes, the motif turning back)
LH: same pattern as bar 1

**Bar 3 — F (VI)**
RH: F₄ – A₄ – C₅ – A₄ (eighth notes, reaching upward)
LH: F₂ – C₃ – A₂ – C₃ – F₂ – C₃ – A₂ – C₃

**Bar 4 — Dm (iv)**
RH: D₄ – F₄ – A₄ – F₄ (eighth notes)
LH: D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂ – D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂

### Bars 5–8: Development and Lift

**Bar 5 — G (VII) or C (III)**
RH: G₄ – B₄ – C₅ – E₅ (eighth notes, the phrase opens upward for a hopeful quality)
LH: G₂ – D₃ – B₂ – D₃ – G₂ – D₃ – B₂ – D₃

**Bar 6 — Am (i)**
RH: E₅ – C₅ – A₄ – C₅ (eighth notes, gently descending)
LH: A₂ – E₃ – C₃ – E₃ (same as bar 1)

**Bar 7 — Dm (iv)**
RH: D₄ – F₄ – A₄ – B₄ (eighth notes, B natural appears as a passing tone reaching toward the dominant)
LH: D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂ – D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂

**Bar 8 — E (V, harmonic minor)**
RH: G#₄ – E₄ (quarter notes, then a half rest — a brief pause before the final phrase, like a breath)
LH: E₂ – B₂ – G#₂ – B₂ (broken chord, then hold)

### Bars 9–12: Return and Close

**Bar 9 — Am (i)**
RH: C₄ – E₄ – G₄ – A₄ (the original motif returns, eighth notes)
LH: A₂ – E₃ – C₃ – E₃ (same opening pattern, like coming home)

**Bar 10 — Am (i)**
RH: G₄ – E₄ – C₄ – E₄
LH: same as bar 9

**Bar 11 — Dm (iv)**
RH: D₄ – F₄ – E₄ – D₄ (eighth notes, a gentle stepwise descent settling down)
LH: D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂ – D₂ – A₂ – F₂ – A₂

**Bar 12 — Am (i)**
RH: C₄ – A₃ (quarter note, then dotted half note — the final A rings out)
LH: A₂ – E₃ – C₃ – E₃ – A₂ (slow the pattern, let the last A₂ sustain)

### Performance Notes

The plagal feeling of Dm–Am at the end (bars 11–12) gives a gentle, hymn-like close that suits a wedding processional or a quiet moment during the ceremony. If you want a stronger ending, replace bar 11 with E major (G#₂ – B₂ – E₃ broken chord in the LH, and add G#₄ in the RH melody) for a V–i authentic cadence.

Use the sustain pedal lightly, changing on each new chord. Keep the tempo steady and unhurried. The LH broken-chord pattern should stay quieter than the RH melody throughout.

If you want to extend it, repeat bars 1–8 as a second verse with the melody up an octave (C₅ – E₅ – G₅ – A₅) for a fuller sound, then play bars 9–12 as the final ending.
